headline: Permanent US FDA approval for goat infant formula after four-year campaign; holds ~24% of growing goat sub-segment with no domestic US competition; potential asset investment or manufacturing partnership in US to shorten lead times
reasoning: After more than four years of effort, Bubs secured permanent FDA access to the US market for its goat infant formula in September. There is no goat infant formula manufactured in the US, so competition comes only from European and Australian importers. Bubs holds approximately 24% of a growing goat sub-segment and also sells bovine and toddler products in the US, with adult nutrition aspirations. The US is described as the 'jewel in the crown' and the company is considering placing manufacturing assets in the US — potentially via partnerships — to better serve retailers and consumers on shorter lead times.
quote: Yeah. Look, that was a huge milestone for us as a business. Um, the team had worked for over four years to secure the permanent access to the US market. So, um, you know, huge market, a high value market, a high growth market as well. In our in our subsegment, there's actually no, um, goat infant formula that's made in the US. So it either comes in from from Europe or Australia. So, um, you know, we're about 24% of a growing goat sub segment in infant formula in the US. So we also have bovine products. We also have toddler products and we have ambitions to look at some adult products. So it's really a beachhead for us from which we can build. But our core focus in the US is that permanency around the goat infant formula. And so we were very excited to secure that permanency. And over time, as our volume grows, um, you know, we'll invest in our business, um, we will expand our business and potentially, um, look at maybe putting some asset into the US so that we can be more responsive for our consumers.
episode_title: Bubs back on track in Vietnam

headline: US market is the growth engine — now ranging in over 10,000 stores across Amazon, Sam's Club, mass and specialty retail, with focus shifting to brand activation and staying on shelf
reasoning: Joe Coote describes the US market as the 'jewel in the crown' and their primary growth engine. Bubs has built distribution across more than 10,000 stores in the US spanning online (Amazon), club stores (Sam's Club), mass retailers, and specialty retailers. The next phase is brand activation and shelf retention to convert distribution into sustained sales and address previous net losses.
quote: Yeah I mean it's our growth engine. Absolutely. As I said, it's the jewel in the crown. So yeah, we absolutely have high ambition for what we can achieve in the US market. As we've shared, we've ranged in over 10,000 stores now, and we're in a good sort of cross section of retail formats. So we have an online presence through Amazon in the US. We're in some of the club stores like Sam's Club and we're in the mass retailers. Um, and we're in the specialty retailers. So yeah, we've got a very broad business built up in the US now with over 10,000 stores. So now it's about activating the brand, staying on shelf and ensuring that we're there for those families that are choosing our products to feed their infants.
episode_title: Bubs back on track in Vietnam

headline: Goat milk formula positioned as premium, easier-to-digest alternative to bovine, with growing penetration in US from near zero five years ago
reasoning: Coote explains that goat milk formula has smaller protein and fat compounds than bovine milk, making it easier for infants to digest and gentler on their stomachs. Consumer feedback consistently highlights that infants who struggle with bovine formula settle better on goat milk. Market penetration varies globally — around 12% in Spain, 6–8% in Australia, and near zero in the US five years ago before Bubs and European competitors entered, suggesting significant runway for growth in the US.
quote: The the compounds, the protein and the fat in the, in the milk tends to simplistically just be a little bit smaller, smaller animal. And so it's easier to digest for the infant. So what we find is a lot of mums will tell us that it's gentle on their infant's tummy. So if an infant is not settling with a bovine product. We quite often hear that the goat product will then allow the infant to digest, and it's a gentle digest. You know, baby sleeps, family is happy. And so that's the preference that the consumers tell us they enjoy with the goat product.
episode_title: Bubs back on track in Vietnam

headline: Relaunching in Vietnam after regulatory hurdles cleared; targeting double-digit growth in a 100-million-person market with strong GDP per capita growth and preference for premium Australian infant formula
reasoning: Bubs paused its Vietnam presence while working through regulatory changes related to carbohydrate labelling on cans. Having resolved those issues with distributor H.C. Farmer, the company has relaunched and Coote visited personally to oversee the relaunch. Vietnam is described as the key growth market in Asia outside China, with a high birth rate and consumer affinity for premium Australian products. The company targets double-digit growth in Vietnam over the next few years, and the market is described as a multi-million dollar opportunity. Bubs' differentiators include the science behind its goat and bovine (Supreme) products.
quote: Yeah. I mean, um, our biggest market, uh, in Asia is China, and we've got a great business in China, and we're very excited by the prospects in China. But, um, the other market that we have a strong presence in is, is Japan. But Vietnam is our key growth market in Asia. So 100 million people, as I mentioned earlier, it's a country that's really got a strong GDP per capita growth. There is a preference for products like like Bob's been a premium Australian infant formula. And so it's really our key growth market in that region. We work with our distributor H.C. farmer. And so we you know, we really feel confident in investing behind our brand and partnering with H.C. farmer to provide those amazing Australian products for the Vietnamese families that choose to feed their babies, our products.
episode_title: Bubs back on track in Vietnam
